name: Bianca Gallagher
life: “I still remember one detour adding a whole hour to an easy shift.” Friday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Bianca stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I work the rail siding. Moving the warehouse shifts half my day onto the road.
appearance: Bianca has short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat, a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a pen clipped inside the neckline. When somebody else has the floor, Bianca folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Bianca takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
family: Essie Good is Bianca’s younger cousin. Bianca is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Essie calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Two portions*, Essie says, “The spare portion is mine. I go home before the register calls me a resident and come back before breakfast.”
connections: Bailey Sato. A rail route and an old wall give the retired shareholder something tangible to show the grandson. Also in the story is Lars James (warehouse trainee).

reactions.response: Bianca asks where existing workers are shown in the finished picture.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Bianca asks the person crying whether they want to go somewhere quieter, leaving them control over the next step.

reactions.response: Bianca asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
